gui.piranport.debug_terminal.description: Adjusts %s; range %s. Input is converted to the internal unit on the server.
Upward buoyancy underwater; default 0.5, range 0.3-1.0. Higher values rise faster.
Horizontal acceleration while walking on water; default 0.03, range 0.0-0.05. Higher values accelerate faster.
Horizontal speed retained after releasing movement; default 0.85, range 0.5-0.95. Lower values stop faster.
Controls the proportion of target armor ignored by armor-piercing projectiles.
Controls the damage multiplier applied by armor-piercing projectiles.
Controls the cooldown between launches for quad torpedo launchers (game ticks).
Controls the cooldown between launches for quintuple torpedo launchers (game ticks).
Controls the cooldown between launches for triple torpedo launchers (game ticks).
Controls whether projectiles can detonate underwater.
Controls the explosion power multiplier when a projectile detonates underwater.
Horizontal velocity retention while a torpedo is falling during an air drop.
Vertical falling speed added per tick during a torpedo air drop.
Horizontal velocity retention during non-air-drop torpedo air-fall fallback.
Vertical falling speed added per tick during non-air-drop torpedo air-fall fallback.
Minimum vertical look component treated as input by a wire-guided torpedo.
Controls the aircraft's maximum carried ammunition.
Controls the base armor used to reduce ordinary incoming damage.
Controls the proportion of target armor ignored by armor-piercing ammunition.
Controls the damage reduction provided by armor plates.
Controls armor toughness used against high-damage attacks.
Controls Artillery Intro Looting Timeout Ticks.
Controls the maximum number of projectile entities allowed at once.
Controls how long a projectile can remain underwater before it is removed.
Controls the wait between two aircraft attacks.
Controls the base damage used by the entity's melee or AI attacks.
Controls the aircraft speed multiplier while approaching and attacking a target.
Controls the accepted position error for trajectory solving; smaller values increase precision.
Controls how many ballistic result entries the cache can retain.
Controls the maximum number of iterations allowed by the ballistic solver.
Controls the maximum number of simulation steps in one trajectory calculation.
Controls the error threshold used to decide that a trajectory has no valid solution.
Controls how many barrels are used by an automatic weapon per trigger.
Controls the ship's base armor before equipment bonuses.
Controls Boss Intro Battle Timeout Ticks.
Controls Boss Intro Defeat Delay Ticks.
Controls Boss Intro Phase Timeout Ticks.
Controls the aircraft speed multiplier during ordinary cruise.
Controls the base damage dealt by this weapon, shell, or attack mode.
Controls final damage as a multiplier of the base value for this ammunition.
Distance at which the torpedo bomber starts descending from approach altitude to the low run altitude, so it is already level when the torpedo run begins.
Controls the random angular spread around the cannon's aim point.
Controls the distance the ship travels per unit of fuel.
Controls flight resistance; larger values make the projectile lose speed faster.
Controls how many uses the equipment or weapon can take before breaking.
Controls ship speed with no equipment load.
Controls explosion power as a multiplier of the base value for this ammunition.
Controls the explosion radius and destructive strength of the ammunition or projectile.
Controls the range at which the fire-control system can lock or assist aiming at targets.
Controls the wait before the cannon can fire again.
Controls the maximum distance at which the entity can find and follow a target.
Controls the aircraft speed multiplier while following a recon aircraft or formation target.
Controls the aircraft's maximum fuel and therefore its sustained flight time.
Controls ship speed while carrying a full equipment load.
Controls the effect of gravity during projectile flight.
Controls the aircraft's health and how much damage it can withstand.
Controls the extra health granted by the ship core.
Controls the horizontal spread of cannon fire.
Controls the projectile speed as it leaves the muzzle.
Controls the wait between automatic weapon triggers.
Controls the aircraft speed multiplier during launch.
Controls the highest elevation angle allowed for the barrel.
Controls the maximum equipment load the ship can carry.

Controls the cannon's maximum firing range (blocks). Beyond this horizontal distance the fire control stops solving for the target and instead solves for a shot landing at this range (not at maximum elevation), showing "Out of range".
Controls the base movement speed used by entity navigation and movement.
Controls the movement-speed multiplier while a mob closes to attack range.
Controls the movement-speed multiplier while a mob chases a target.
Controls the movement-speed multiplier when a mob has no movement target.
Controls the movement-speed multiplier while a mob follows its navigation path.
Controls the movement-speed multiplier while a mob moves in water or a bubble column.
Controls the damage dealt when the aircraft payload hits.
Controls the aircraft's base speed during launch, cruise, and return.
Controls the longest lifetime of a pellet or fragment entity.
Controls whether calculated ballistic solutions are cached to avoid repeated work.

Horizontal distance to the target at which the aircraft releases. Dive bombers default to 2 blocks; torpedo bombers default to 30 blocks.
Controls the time required to complete one reload.

Speed used to pull away from a target that is closer than the run entry distance before the torpedo run.

message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_bra: Long-term contact is established. Different supplies can now open support branches, not just one-time rewards.
Reports suit recon, repair kits suit maintenance, and experience shells suit drills. Do not treat every supply as plain loot.
Fuel connects air cover, shards suit research, and flags can extend supply beacons.
Each branch is recorded the first time it is completed. Repeat deliveries still provide smaller support.
All six support branches are connected. This route is not merely passable now; it can be operated.
Recon, maintenance, drill, air cover, research, and supply are all filed. Next, tune equipment and formation until they feel natural.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_cal: After maintenance, the only thing missing is a route beacon. A dungeon key can calibrate the abyssal coordinates.
If the core is ready, hand it over and I will finish the final calibration.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_com: Rules of engagement are set to standby. I will not start fights on my own.
The joint route is stable. I can keep providing supplies, trade, and combat support.
The abyssal flagship will not simply wait. Prepare your equipment and sortie decisively.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_fac: C-line rigging values array stability. When the talisman light rises, keep the formation from spreading too far.
I will mark the supply line on the near-sea side. You take the fire window; I will keep an exit open.
For an abyssal base, read the tide line before the enemy group. Good shelling comes from calm preparation.
E-line longbow motion needs lead. The farther the target, the less you can stare only at the center of the sight.
Sea fog can fool the eye, but not the record. Read impact point, smoke trail, and delayed sound together.
A carrier deck is not background decoration. Stable airspace gives the fleet another margin of safety.
F-line rigging favors diagonal thrusts. Do not press head-on forever; a new angle opens gaps in abyssal formations.
The rapier-style launch is about decisiveness: confirm, launch, reposition. Do not hesitate in one place for long.
Supply points inside abyssal bases matter. If you can take resources, do not only think about flattening walls.
G-line mechanical arrays like exact numbers. Turret speed, spread, and reload rhythm should be judged together.
Submarine routes need patience. In abyssal fog, the danger is not seeing the enemy; it is forgetting where you are.
If the trajectory looks wrong, check range and elevation first. Instinct helps, but records are steadier.
I-line catapult motions should feel light. Once aircraft leave deck, the next cycle should already be ready.
Supply matters as much as speed. Getting out is only the first step; returning with results completes the sortie.
Large-caliber guns announce your position. After firing, take a better angle.
J-line rigging rewards clean launch motions: set the heading first, then smooth the deck wind.
The bow-style launch is not a pose. It folds sightline, wind, and sortie rhythm into one line.
Against fast abyssal units, do not chase damage alone. Lay flare and smoke first; hits become more reliable.
U-line firearm launches are loud, but smoke and blast can also cut the sightline open again.
If the target is too far, watch the impact and correct. Shells tell the truth; they are simply loud about it.
Keep a fuel margin for carrier catapults. Emptying the last barrel makes retreat ugly.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_fol: I will follow your route and keep formation.
The final step needs any faction flag as a contact signal. A flag is not decoration; it is route authority.
Once the faction signal is established, abyssal actions can become long-term support instead of one-off sorties.
After you hand me a flag, support will be tracked as recon, maintenance, drill, air cover, research, and supply.
The fog after a flagship sinks leaves a reverse wake. Bring the post-battle report and I can chart the next coordinate.
The abyssal flagship has clear phase changes. The fuller the review, the safer the next expedition.
If the flagship is down, do not discard the report. It contains long-term clues for abyssal-world operations.
The post-battle coordinate is still drifting. A chaos shard can anchor the residual beacon.
A shard is not just material. Stabilize its resonance before we turn it into expedition support.
I will write the shard frequency into port records so supply, recon, and maintenance can connect.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_hol: I will hold this position. Use the command sword if you need me to move.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_int: The abyssal fog records are still incomplete. If you find an operation report, bring it to me first.
Sortieing without intel is too risky. Start with clues from abyssal units and ruins.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_pre: The route in the report is usable, but the sortie kit needs preparation. Bring an emergency repair kit.
A supply unit may still have repair tools. Bring fuel and it may trade.
message.piranport.ship_girl_dialogue_rap: Our rapport is high now. I can read your pause before firing, your reload rhythm, and your retreat route.
Port operations are not built on one victory. Return steadily, resupply steadily, sortie steadily. That is a long front.
Use the command sword if you need me to follow. If you need me to hold, I will treat this place as a temporary anchorage.

piranport.book.advanced.aircraft_types.p: $(bold)Torpedo bomber profile:$() torpedo bombers drop to sea-skimming level flight, pre-solve lead 20-30 blocks out, and release the aerial torpedo at the drop point; the torpedo runs straight just under the surface, unguided.$(br2)That level run is the main AA window; dive bombers instead attack in a shallow dive at close range.
piranport.book.arsenal.crafting.blueprin: $(bold)Blueprint rules:$()$(br)• $(bold)Initial$() gear crafts freely$(br)• $(bold)Standard$() needs a $(item)Standard Weapon Blueprint$() (craftable)$(br)• $(bold)Improved/Advanced$() need their tier blueprints — only from dungeon rewards, chests, or the weaponsmith villager$(br)• Blueprints sit in the workbench slot and are $(bold)not consumed$(); the creative blueprint substitutes for any tier$(br2)$(bold)Uncraftables:$() some heavy guns (triple 460mm class) and special weapons never enter the workbench — get them from dungeon bosses or villager trades.
piranport.book.arsenal.crafting.p1: $(bold)Weapon Workbench:$() Right-click to open GUI. 5 tabs (Cannons/Torpedo Launchers/Missile Launchers/Depth Charges/Aircraft). Select a recipe, insert materials, and click Craft. Some advanced weapons require $(item)Blueprints$(). Crafting takes time; collect the result when done.
piranport.book.arsenal.crafting.p2: $(bold)Ammo Workbench:$() Craft various ammo types (shells, torpedoes, missiles, depth charges).$(br)$(br)$(bold)Reload Facility:$() Insert an empty launcher and matching ammo to load it. Works with cannons, torpedo launchers, and missile launchers.
piranport.book.arsenal.depth_charges.adv: Crafting recipe for the Advanced Depth Charge Launcher.
piranport.book.arsenal.depth_charges.imp: Crafting recipe for the Improved Depth Charge Launcher.
piranport.book.arsenal.depth_charges.p1: $(item)Depth Charge Launchers$() deploy $(item)Depth Charges$() against underwater targets. Three models:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Depth Charge Launcher$() — 1 charge, single drop$(br)$(bold)DC Launcher Improved$() — 2 charges, fore-aft spread$(br)$(bold)DC Launcher Advanced$() — 3 charges, triangle spread$(br)$(br)Depth charges sink automatically and detonate via $(bold)proximity fuze$() when near a target, dealing area magic damage.
piranport.book.arsenal.missiles.p1: Missiles come in three types:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Anti-Ship Missiles:$() $(item)SY-1 Launcher$() (30 damage +6 AP, burst 2) and $(item)MK14 Harpoon Launcher$() (24 damage, burst 4). Right-click to launch; auto-tracks nearest target ahead (excludes underwater targets and containers), or tracks fire-control locked target.
piranport.book.arsenal.missiles.p2: $(bold)Anti-Air Missiles:$() $(item)Terrier Launcher$(), $(item)Sea Dart Launcher$(), $(item)Seacat Launcher$(). With $(bold)[H]$() auto-launch enabled, they auto-fire when airborne enemies are within 32 blocks, prioritizing fire-control locked targets.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Rockets:$() $(item)Ship Rocket Launcher$(), fires straight with no guidance.$(br)$(br)Unfilled launchers show an empty durability bar as a reminder.
piranport.book.arsenal.special.gungnir: Gungnir is a powerful throwing weapon that deals high damage to enemies.
piranport.book.arsenal.special.p1: $(bold)Combat Items:$(br)$(item)Damage Control$() — Clears all debuffs and extinguishes fire$(br)$(item)Repair Kit$() — Hold right-click on a mob to continuously heal$(br)$(item)Smoke Candle$() — Deploys a smoke screen block$(br)$(item)Flare Launcher$() — Fires a flare that creates light on blocks, makes mobs glow on hit
piranport.book.arsenal.special.p2: $(bold)Special Weapons:$(br)$(item)Mysterious Weapon$() (Railgun) — Gravity-ignoring high-speed projectile$(br)$(item)Gungnir$() — Throwing weapon$(br)$(item)Eugen's Ship Shield$() — Blocks 150° frontal arc$(br)$(item)Hatsuyuki's Main Gun$() — Axe-type weapon$(br)$(br)$(bold)Equipment:$(br)$(item)Kirin-class Headband$() — Permanent invisibility$(br)$(item)Football Superstar Set$() (4-piece) — Experience Boost buff
piranport.book.arsenal.special.p3: $(bold)Type-3 Shells$()$(br2)Type-3 shells are special rounds that scatter multiple submunitions on detonation, forming a barrage.$(br2)$(bold)Best against:$()$(br)• Dense enemy groups$(br)• Intercepting aircraft squadrons$(br)• Area suppression
piranport.book.arsenal.special.p4: $(bold)Character Weapons$()$(br2)• $(item)Richelieu's Saber$(): melee, 1520 durability, +8 damage$(br)• $(item)Hatsuyuki's Main Gun$(): axe-class, +11 damage$(br)• $(item)Prinz Eugen's Shield$(): 150-degree block arc
piranport.book.aviation.aircraft.p1: Six aircraft types: $(item)Fighter$() (hovers and fires bullets; air targets only), $(item)Dive Bomber$() (dives close and drops a bomb), $(item)Torpedo Bomber$() (drops to sea-skimming level flight, pre-solves lead, and releases an aerial torpedo that runs straight underwater), $(item)Level Bomber$() (drops bombs from above the target), $(item)ASW Aircraft$() (drops depth charges, targets only submarines/aquatic mobs), and $(item)Saiun$() (see Recon entry).
piranport.book.aviation.aircraft.p2: While transformed, hold an aircraft item and $(bold)right-click$() to launch it. Aircraft draw fuel and matching ammo from your inventory: $(item)Bullets$() for fighters, $(item)Aerial Bombs$() for bombers, and $(item)Aerial Torpedoes$() for torpedo bombers.
piranport.book.aviation.asw.p1: $(item)ASW Aircraft$() specialize in attacking underwater targets. Currently available: $(item)Swordfish Mk3$() and $(item)TBF (ASW)$().$(br)$(br)$(bold)Attack behavior:$() Only attacks submarines and aquatic mobs. Flies over the target and drops $(item)Depth Charges$().$(br)$(br)$(bold)Sonar detection:$() ASW aircraft scan for underwater entities every second. Detected targets are highlighted with a $(bold)yellow outline$(). Sonar highlighting is independent of fire-control highlights.
piranport.book.aviation.fire_control.p1: While transformed: $(bold)Mouse Middle$() adds crosshair target (80-block range); $(bold)Sneak+Middle$() replaces with a single target; $(bold)Sneak+Middle$() with no entity under the crosshair cancels all locks. Locked targets shown in top-right HUD.
piranport.book.aviation.fire_control.p2: $(bold)Target cap:$() the lock list holds at most $(bold)4$() targets; the server validates 80-block range, line of sight and liveness, and dead targets are removed automatically. Once full, new picks are ignored until you sneak+middle-click to clear.
piranport.book.aviation.fire_control.p3: $(bold)Prediction HUD:$() with a cannon in hand and a locked target, a white HUD circle marks the predicted impact point — it turns green when your crosshair covers it, and warns when the point exceeds the gun's aiming range.$(br2)With a ship core off-hand and a torpedo launcher in hand, a white lead line marks the predicted hit point; multi-tube launchers show a spread fan.
piranport.book.aviation.fire_control.p4: $(bold)Auto-launch/AA [H]:$() $(bold)H$() toggles both automatic fighter launch and automatic SAM fire; with it off, launch planes manually by right-click. Status shows on the action bar.
piranport.book.aviation.fire_control.p5: $(bold)Highlight & cleanup:$() locked targets glow red — below vanilla highlight, above sonar yellow.$(br2)Lock data lives server-side and is wiped on logout. No-GUI mode intentionally lacks grouping and auto-launch.
piranport.book.aviation.recon.p1: The $(item)Saiun$() is a non-combat aircraft used for scouting. It carries no weapons or ammo. After launching, recon view engages automatically — your camera follows the aircraft in real time. Press $(bold)[V]$() to exit. The recon plane force-loads chunks around it so you can see distant terrain. Useful for spotting enemy positions before committing to an attack.
piranport.book.cannons.advanced.p1: $(bold)VT Shell (Proximity Fuze):$() Small caliber only. Follows the same trajectory as HE shells but detonates automatically near the target. Effective against fast-moving targets.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Type 3 Shell (Sanshiki):$() Available in Small/Medium/Large caliber. Fires a spread of 64 pellets in a cone pattern. Each pellet deals 1/4 of the equivalent HE shell's damage. Effective against dense target groups or aircraft squadrons.
piranport.book.cannons.basics.craft: All guns and torpedo launchers are made at the $(item)Weapon Workbench$(). Initial-tier gear needs no blueprint; Standard/Improved/Advanced gear needs the matching tier blueprint in the blueprint slot (not consumed, copyable in the Blueprint Chest).
piranport.book.cannons.basics.large: Materials scale with caliber family and barrel count: small guns use iron and copper, medium adds aluminum, large adds diamonds. Higher tiers add gold, diamonds and netherite scrap, and take longer to build.
piranport.book.cannons.basics.medium: The $(item)Standard Weapon Blueprint$() is crafted from paper, iron, aluminum and redstone. $(item)Improved$() and $(item)Advanced$() blueprints come only from trophy trades with the weaponsmith villager or dungeon first-clear rewards.
piranport.book.cannons.basics.ops: $(bold)Switch Ammo [Tab]:$() Press Tab to open the ammo selection overlay. Move your mouse to pick between HE and AP shells (and special shells like VT/Sanshiki if available). Release Tab to confirm the selection.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Reload [R]:$() Press R to manually reload your current gun from ammo in your inventory.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Scope:$() Right-click while transformed to enter scope view — a zoomed first-person perspective with a crosshair for precision aiming.
piranport.book.cannons.basics.p1: Guns come in three caliber families: small (<5 in), medium (5 to <13 in) and large (>=13 in). Shells must match the family. Barrel count determines ammo consumed per salvo.$(br)$(br)$(item)HE Shells$() cause area explosions. $(item)AP Shells$() deal higher armor-piercing damage.
piranport.book.cannons.basics.range: $(bold)Max horizontal range:$() some cannons define $(bold)maxHorizontalRange$(). Aiming beyond it solves elevation at the capped distance and shows an out-of-range warning, but the shell still flies at full muzzle velocity — it is never cut off mid-flight.$(br2)Cannons without the field can aim out to their physical range.
piranport.book.cat.arsenal.desc: Missiles, depth charges, special equipment, and weapon crafting facilities.
piranport.book.cat.aviation.desc: Carrier aircraft, ground-attack toggles, and fire control.
piranport.book.cat.combat.desc: Combat effects, buff foods, and battlefield tactics.
piranport.book.cat.config.desc: Key bindings, client settings, and debug tools.
piranport.book.cat.cooking.desc: Crops, processing stations, and naval cuisine.
piranport.book.cat.dungeon.desc: Sea area sorties and node-based combat.
piranport.book.cat.equipment.desc: Armor plates, engines, and special gear.
piranport.book.cat.ruins.desc: Four types of ruin structures scattered across the ocean: Portal Ruins, Supply Depots, Outposts, and Abyssal Bases.
piranport.book.cat.support.desc: Sonar, smoke screens, flares, and reload facilities.
piranport.book.combat.buff_foods.p1: $(item)Chicken Tatsuta$() — $(bold)Reload Boost I$() for 180s.$(br)$(br)$(item)Torpedo Juice$() — $(bold)Hunger II + Reload Boost II + Fire Resistance I$(); returns bottle.$(br)$(br)$(item)Tempura$() — $(bold)Evasion I$() for 180s.$(br)$(br)$(item)Kvass$() — $(bold)Slowness I + Slow Falling I + Evasion II$() for 120s; returns bottle.$(br)$(br)Cook these at the $(item)Cooking Pot$() using standard ingredients.
piranport.book.combat.effects.p1: $(bold)Flooding:$() Applied by torpedo hits. Slows and damages the target over time.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Reload Boost:$() Shortens weapon cooldowns and bow/crossbow draw time to 0.9/0.8/0.7x at levels I-III. Obtained from food like $(item)Chicken Tatsuta$() or $(item)Torpedo Juice$().$(br)$(br)$(bold)Evasion:$() Grants a dodge chance (10%/20%/30% at levels I/II/III) while transformed. Obtained from $(item)Tempura$() or $(item)Kvass$().$(br)$(br)$(bold)Flammable:$() Fire hazard debuff when loading fuel (disabled by default in config).
piranport.book.cooking.crops.p1: Eight crops can be grown: $(item)Tomato$(), $(item)Soybean$(), $(item)Chili$(), $(item)Onion$(), $(item)Rice$(), $(item)Lettuce$(), $(item)Garlic$(), and $(item)Pineapple$(). Seeds drop from tall grass or wandering traders. Plant on farmland; Rice grows in waterlogged soil.
piranport.book.cooking.crops.p2: Harvest crops when mature. Tomatoes, onions, rice, and other crops can be used to cook various dishes. Some crops can be ground into flour or powder using the stone mill for more complex recipes.
piranport.book.cooking.salt_rice.p1: $(bold)Salt Evaporation:$() Place a $(item)Water Source$() block directly above a lit $(item)Furnace$(). After 10 seconds, the water converts to a $(item)Salt Block$(). Flowing water above a furnace produces $(item)Salt Chips$() instead.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Rice Paddies:$() $(item)Rice$() must be planted on waterlogged farmland — place water and plant rice seeds on the flooded block. If the water is removed, the crop breaks.$(br)$(br)Salt no longer generates naturally; furnace evaporation is the stable source.
piranport.book.cooking.stations.p1: $(bold)Stone Mill:$() Right-click to open. Grind crops into flour, powder, and paste. Accepts up to 4 ingredients and produces 1-2 outputs.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Cutting Board:$() Right-click to place an ingredient, then right-click repeatedly to cut. Shift+right-click to retrieve.
piranport.book.cooking.stations.p2: $(bold)Cooking Pot:$() Place over a heat source (fire, campfire, magma, lava). Right-click to open GUI. Add ingredients; the pot cooks automatically when heated. Recipes combine 1-9 inputs into a single food output.
piranport.book.cooking.stations.p3: All cooking pot dishes cook automatically as long as a heat source (fire, lava, etc.) is present. Put the ingredients in the pot and wait for cooking to finish.
piranport.book.cooking.world_dishes.appl: Bake the Apple Pie Dough over a Campfire.
piranport.book.cooking.world_dishes.p1: The mod includes a rich variety of dishes from around the world, all crafted at the $(item)Cooking Pot$().$(br)$(br)$(bold)Chinese:$() $(item)Dongpo Pork$(), $(item)Deluxe Baozi$(), $(item)Tangyuan$(), $(item)Assorted Char Siu Fried Rice$()$(br)$(bold)Japanese:$() $(item)Soba Noodle$(), $(item)Tempura Soba$(), $(item)Yokan$()$(br)$(bold)German:$() $(item)Schweinshaxe$(), $(item)Thuringer Rostbratwurst$(), $(item)Thuringer Rostbratwurst und Bier$(), $(item)Weisswurst mit Bagel$(), $(item)Black Forest Gateau$()
piranport.book.cooking.world_dishes.p2: $(bold)Russian:$() $(item)Borscht$(), $(item)Okroshka$(), $(item)Russian Dumpling$(), $(item)Rye Bread (Dish)$(), $(item)New Rye Bread$(), $(item)Kvass (Dish)$()$(br)$(bold)British:$() $(item)Yorkshire Pudding$(), $(item)Eggs Benedict$(), $(item)Black Tea Scone$(), $(item)Black Tea Sandwich$(), $(item)Royal Naval Salted Beef$()$(br)$(bold)Others:$() $(item)Bouillabaisse$(), $(item)Salami Pizza$(), $(item)Venice Cuttlefish Noodles$(), $(item)Macaron$(), $(item)Tarte Tatin$(), $(item)Double/Triple Shell Burger$(), $(item)Barbecue$(), etc.$(br)$(br)All dishes can be placed on the ground for shared eating.
piranport.book.cooking.world_dishes.pizz: Cook the Salami Pizza Dough on a Campfire.
piranport.book.cooking.world_dishes.rice: Steam raw rice over a Campfire.
piranport.book.dungeon.basics.p1: Obtain a $(item)Dungeon Key$() and find a $(item)Dungeon Lectern$(). Right-click the lectern with a key to open the sortie screen. Choose a chapter and stage, then press $(bold)Sortie$() to enter. Each stage has multiple nodes connected by $(item)Portals$(). Walk into a portal to advance to the next node.
piranport.book.dungeon.basics.p2: At each node, defeat all enemies to proceed. Collect supplies from $(item)Loot Ships$() along the way. If you fall in combat, you may revive by consuming a $(item)Totem of Undying$(), or give up and return to the lobby. Use a $(item)Town Scroll$() to exit the dungeon early. First clear of each stage grants bonus rewards. Your progress is saved on the $(item)Dungeon Key$().
piranport.book.dungeon.keys.craft_ch1: Chapter 1 Wooden Key: 4x Key Fragment · Ch.1.
piranport.book.dungeon.keys.craft_ch2: Chapter 2 Stone Key: 4x Key Fragment · Ch.2 + Deployment Medal · Ch.1 (medal kept). Later chapters work the same way.
piranport.book.dungeon.keys.p1: The $(item)Dungeon Key$() is both ticket and progress carrier — seven chapters, seven keys: Wooden/Stone/Copper/Iron/Golden/Diamond/Emerald.$(br2)The Chapter 1 Wooden Key is crafted from 4x $(item)Key Fragment · Ch.1$() in a 2x2. Chapter 2+ keys need 4 fragments plus the previous chapter's $(item)Deployment Medal$(), which is not consumed.
piranport.book.dungeon.keys.p2: $(bold)Fragment sources:$()$(br)• Late-chapter mainline clears (4-2, 5-4, 6-2, 6-4, 7-2, ...)$(br)• Ruin chests in supply depots, outposts and abyssal bases$(br2)Abandoned portal ruin chests contain a finished Ch.1 key. A copy recipe turns a used key into a fresh blank key of the same chapter while keeping the original's progress — that's how you re-farm a stage.
piranport.book.dungeon.keys.p3: $(bold)Lectern glow:$()$(br)• White = empty, needs a key$(br)• Red = instance building, or the player cap is reached$(br)• Green = enterable$(br2)Bare-hand right-click on a keyed lectern removes the key. Breaking the lectern always drops it. With progress saved, right-click offers Continue/Restart. Death or clearing returns you to the lectern you entered from; losing the key loses the progress.
piranport.book.dungeon.nodes.p1: Each stage is a node graph linked by sea-surface portals. Node types:$(br)• $(bold)Battle$(): clear all enemies$(br)• $(bold)Boss$(): kill the flagship$(br)• $(bold)Resource$(): supplies and totems$(br)• $(bold)Cost$(): pay items to pass$(br2)Cleared end nodes light a gate to the boss instead of ejecting you.
piranport.book.dungeon.nodes.p2: $(bold)Abyssal bestiary:$()$(br)• $(item)Abyssal Destroyer$(): rapid guns + torpedo salvos$(br)• $(item)Abyssal Light Cruiser$(): medium guns; high-tier also AA guns$(br)• $(item)Abyssal Heavy Cruiser$(): armored wall, use AP$(br)• $(item)Abyssal Battle Cruiser$() / $(item)Battleship$(): heavy salvos with reload windows$(br)• $(item)Abyssal Light/Fleet Carrier$(): aircraft strikes$(br)• $(item)Abyssal Submarine$(): underwater torpedoes — depth charges are the reliable answer
piranport.book.dungeon.nodes.p3: $(bold)Formation rules:$() abyssal fleets sail in formation — big ships first, high-tier first within a class; the lead ship steers, successors take over when it sinks. Submarines run 1-2 ship ambush packs. Bosses act alone with escort fleets.$(br2)Kills drop $(item)Loot Ships$(): right-click the floating crate ship before it despawns.
piranport.book.dungeon.nodes.p4: $(bold)Branching gates:$() one node may open several gates, each labeled with destination and requirement (hull type, escort count, carried items, luck). Only satisfied gates are lit; a dark gate won't teleport and tells you what's missing. A default gate always stays lit so a boss path exists. Gates evaluate per player, not per instance.$(br2)$(bold)Multiplayer:$() up to 4 players online per instance; enemy HP and wave counts scale with players present at node activation and don't rescale mid-node.
piranport.book.dungeon.rewards.p1: Clearing the boss node clears the stage. Rewards go to every player inside the boss node at the moment of the kill — no damage contribution required, and replays pay out again.$(br2)Each stage declares its rewards (first_clear_rewards): material packs (iron/aluminum/gunpowder/fuel drums), the chapter $(item)Deployment Medal$(), and on later chapters $(item)Key Fragments$() and weapon blueprints.
piranport.book.dungeon.rewards.p2: $(bold)Mainline highlights:$()$(br)• Medals: every clear grants the chapter medal — required to craft the next chapter's key$(br)• Blueprints: some stages put exclusive weapon blueprints in the reward/loot pools$(br)• Fragments: chapter-final stages from 4-2 onward grant next-chapter fragments$(br2)Resource nodes and loot ships pay out independently of the clear reward.
piranport.book.dungeon.rewards.p3: $(bold)Event stage:$() 'Golden Kitty Target Practice' is a standalone event chapter whose battleship boss barely fights back — a moving target dummy that pays out XP shells and toast.$(br2)The mainline has 7 chapters / 30 stages: chapters 5 and 7 have 5 stages, the rest 4 each, difficulty rising per chapter.
piranport.book.dungeon.rewards.p4: $(bold)Failure & retry:$() annihilation has no fail condition. On death spend a totem to revive, or return to the lectern and re-enter from a checkpoint; enemies, chests and progress are not reset by leaving. A $(item)Town Scroll$() exits early back to the ruins.$(br2)No death penalty is the core design — the only cost is travel time.
piranport.book.intro.debug.p1: Debug tools are available for server operators and mod developers.$(br)$(br)Right-click the Debug Terminal to open its parameter and control pages. The control page has debug mode, cooldown override, hit notifications, and log snapshot buttons. Shift-right-click the terminal to write a snapshot directly.$(br)$(br)Debug mode writes detailed logs and shows extra cannon tooltip data.
piranport.book.intro.debug.p2: The parameter page lists targets inside categories; open a target to view its parameters, and use the search box to filter targets in the selected category. The page shows server values beside editable drafts. Confirm one entry or save all drafts explicitly; refresh discards drafts. Reset clears overrides. CSV import and export use files on the server.$(br)$(br)Creative Blueprint can substitute for a blueprint in the Weapon Workbench.
piranport.book.intro.fuel.craft_smelting: Ship Fuel can also be obtained by smelting Charcoal in a Furnace.
piranport.book.intro.fuel.p1: Ship Cores require $(item)Fuel$() to maintain transformation. Fuel can be added using: $(item)Coal$() (+1), $(item)Blaze Rod$() (+1), or $(item)Fuel$() item (+1). Place fuel items onto a Ship Core to refuel.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Fuel capacity:$()$(br)Small: 10 / Medium: 20 / Large: 30 / Submarine: 10$(br)$(br)Fuel is consumed by distance while transformed. When fuel runs out, transformation ends automatically. Aircraft tooltips show a single $(item)Ready$() / $(item)Not Loaded$() state covering both fuel and payload.
piranport.book.intro.fuel.p2: Aircraft and ship cores now share the same $(item)Fuel$(); fuel no longer exists as a separate item. Aircraft automatically draw fuel from your inventory before launch, or you can drag fuel onto an aircraft item to load it manually.
piranport.book.intro.fuel.p3: $(bold)Weight & fuel burn:$() every armament has Weight — a combined measure of mass, space and power. The ratio of used Weight to total capacity drives your speed and transformation fuel burn: heavier loads sail slower and drink faster, and overloading adds penalties.$(br2)$(item)Consumables$() (damage control, rations) don't count toward Weight.$(br2)$(bold)Aircraft servicing:$() launch auto-draws matching ammo and fuel from your inventory; with auto-resupply off, drag fuel onto the plane item manually.
piranport.book.intro.getting_started.p1: Welcome to Piran Port! Follow these steps and you'll be firing guns within half an hour:$(br)$(br)$(bold)1. Mine:$() Find $(item)Bauxite Ore$() on surfaces or in mountains. Breaking it drops $(item)Raw Aluminum$() (Silk Touch drops the ore itself). Smelt to get $(item)Aluminum Ingots$().$(br)$(bold)2. Gather Salt:$() Zombies occasionally drop $(item)Salt$(); the stable source is evaporating water above a lit furnace (see "Salt & Rice").
piranport.book.intro.getting_started.p2: $(bold)3. Craft a Core:$() Use aluminum + salt + wood to craft a $(item)Ship Core$(). Start with $(item)Small Ship Core$() — cheap and agile. You can upgrade later.$(br)$(bold)4. Equip Weapons:$() Put cannons, torpedo launchers, missile launchers, or aircraft on your hotbar, and keep matching ammo in your inventory. Drag fuel items onto the ship core to refuel it.$(br)$(bold)5. Transform & Fight:$() $(bold)Place the core in your offhand$() to automatically transform into a kansen. Hold a weapon or aircraft and $(bold)right-click$() to fire or launch.
piranport.book.intro.getting_started.p3: $(bold)Key Reference:$()$(br)$(item)R$() — Manual reload$(br)$(item)Tab$() — Switch ammo type$(br)$(item)Mouse Middle$() — Add target to fire control$(br)$(item)Sneak+Middle$() — Replace with single target$(br)$(item)Sneak+Middle (no target)$() — Clear all locks$(br)$(item)H$() — Auto-launch / auto-AA toggle$(br)$(item)V$() — Exit recon view$(br)$(br)$(bold)Developers:$() Use the Debug Terminal for debug controls and parameters.$(br)$(br)Every feature has a detailed entry later.
piranport.book.intro.getting_started.p4: All keys above are rebindable in Controls settings under the $(bold)Piran Port$() category.
piranport.book.intro.materials.bauxite_b: Blasting Raw Aluminum in a Blast Furnace is faster, halving the smelting time.
piranport.book.intro.materials.bauxite_s: Smelting Raw Aluminum in a Furnace yields Aluminum Ingots, with each ore producing 1 Aluminum Ingot.
piranport.book.intro.materials.p1: $(item)Aluminum Ingot$() is a core material in this mod, used to craft Ship Cores and various weapons and equipment. Aluminum Ingots are obtained by smelting $(item)Raw Aluminum$().$(br)$(br)$(item)Bauxite Ore$() generates on the surface and within mountains, dropping $(item)Raw Aluminum$() when mined. Using the Silk Touch enchantment lets you obtain the ore block directly.
piranport.book.intro.materials.raw_blast: Smelting Raw Aluminum in a Blast Furnace is faster and better suited to mass production.
piranport.book.intro.materials.raw_smelt: Raw Aluminum can also be smelted into an Aluminum Ingot in a Furnace.
piranport.book.intro.overview.craft: Four ship core types available (Small/Medium/Large/Submarine). Larger cores hold more weapons and have higher load capacity. Each core has a different fuel capacity.
piranport.book.intro.overview.large_craf: Large cores offer maximum weapon slots and load capacity, capable of equipping heavy guns and full aviation squadrons.
piranport.book.intro.overview.medium_cra: Medium cores provide more weapon slots and load capacity, suitable for versatile combat with multiple weapon types.
piranport.book.intro.overview.p1: Piran Port is a Warship Girls R themed mod. To begin, mine $(item)Bauxite Ore$() for $(item)Aluminum Ingots$() (drops $(item)Raw Aluminum$() without Silk Touch) and collect $(item)Salt$(). Craft a $(item)Ship Core$() — Small, Medium, Large, or Submarine — then put weapons on your hotbar and keep ammo in your inventory before sortie.
piranport.book.intro.skins.p1: $(item)Skin Cores$() change your character's appearance. $(bold)Shift+Right-click$() a Skin Core to equip the skin. $(bold)Shift+Right-click$() the same skin again to remove it (core is not consumed). Switching to a different skin returns the old core to your inventory and consumes the new one.$(br)$(br)21 named Skin Cores are available (Kumano, Nürnberg, U-1405 and more) — crafted via flag dyeing. Skin state is synced across all players.
piranport.book.intro.transform.medium_co: Crafting recipe for the Medium Ship Core.
piranport.book.intro.transform.p1: Ship cores transform in one mode:$(br)$(br)$(bold)Offhand Mode:$() Place the ship core in your offhand — the rigging activates automatically.$(br)$(br)Your speed decreases based on total equipment weight. Enhancement slots accept $(item)Armor Plates$() for bonus defense and extra weight.
piranport.book.intro.transform.p2: When a fueled core is in the configured slot, transformation starts automatically; removing the core or running out of fuel ends it automatically. While transformed, hold a cannon, torpedo launcher, missile launcher, or aircraft and $(bold)right-click$() to attack or launch. Drag enhancement items onto the ship core in your inventory to store them; right-click the core with an empty cursor to retrieve the last stored enhancement.
piranport.book.intro.villager_trades.p1: $(bold)Piran Port professions:$() the mod adds three independent professions on their own workstations:$(br2)• $(bold)Weaponsmith$() (Weapon Workbench): sells basic guns and torpedoes, buys aluminum/fuel for emeralds, and trades medium/improved/advanced blueprints plus special weapons for trophies$(br)• $(bold)Quartermaster$() (Ammo Workbench): buys gunpowder/copper, sells HE/AP shells and 533mm torpedoes$(br)• $(bold)Farmer$() (Stone Mill): buys mod crops for emeralds
piranport.book.intro.villager_trades.p2: $(bold)Tip:$() the weaponsmith's blueprint trades want $(item)trophy$() items (abyssal drops), not emeralds — he is the steady source of improved and advanced blueprints. The quartermaster is your ammo supply line before your ammo workbench can keep up.
piranport.book.landing: A guide to ship rigging, weapons, cooking, aviation, combat buffs, and dungeon sorties. Craft it with a Book and an Aluminum Ingot.
piranport.book.name: Piran Port Navigation Manual
piranport.book.ruins.enemies.p1: The abyssal forces consist of 9 ship types:$(br)§lSupply§r — Harmless supply unit$(br)§lDestroyer§r — Fast light cannons$(br)§lLight Cruiser§r — Cannons + torpedoes$(br)§lHeavy Cruiser§r — Heavy guns + high armor$(br)§lBattle Cruiser§r — High-damage tracking shells
piranport.book.ruins.enemies.p2: §lBattleship§r — Strongest cannons + highest defense$(br)§lLight Carrier§r — Launches a few aircraft$(br)§lCarrier§r — Large aircraft squadrons$(br)§lSubmarine§r — Underwater stealth + torpedo attacks$(br)$(br)Abyssal NPCs have fleet alert AI — attacking one may alert the entire fleet!
piranport.book.ruins.loot.p1: Each ruin type contains different tiers of loot:$(br)$(br)§lPortal Ruins§r — Basic materials, plus finished Chapter 1 wooden keys$(br)§lSupply Depots§r — Small equipment, fuel, national flags, dungeon lecterns$(br)§lOutposts§r — Medium equipment, aircraft, exp shells, key fragments
piranport.book.ruins.loot.p2: $(bold)Abyssal Base$() — all-tier equipment, key fragments, fuel barrels (common)$(br)$(br)There are 9 key fragments (α~ι), used to craft dungeon keys. Flags are used for skin crafting.
piranport.book.ruins.overview.p1: Across the ocean biomes, you will find four types of ruin structures.$(br)$(br)§lPortal Ruins§r — Ancient portal frames on the ocean floor. No enemies, but frame materials can be collected.$(br)§lSupply Depots§r — Small building remnants with light enemy guards and basic loot.
piranport.book.ruins.overview.p2: §lOutposts§r — Medium military facilities with runway structures, more abyssal NPCs, and richer loot.$(br)§lAbyssal Bases§r — Large bases found only in deep ocean biomes. Multiple runways, many high-level enemies, and the best loot and rare materials.$(br)$(br)Make sure to equip your rigging before exploring!
piranport.book.torpedoes.basics.craft: Triple launcher fires 3 torpedoes in a ±4° spread. Larger launchers spread wider.
piranport.book.torpedoes.basics.p1: Torpedo launchers (Triple/Quad/Quintuple) fire 533mm or 610mm torpedoes in a spread pattern. Torpedoes travel across water surfaces and inflict the $(item)Flooding$() debuff on hit. They self-destruct after 1 minute if they miss.
piranport.book.torpedoes.basics.quad_cra: Quad torpedo launcher fires 4 torpedoes simultaneously with maximum spread angle and firepower density.
piranport.book.torpedoes.basics.quint_cr: Quintuple torpedo launcher fires 5 torpedoes simultaneously with the highest firepower output.
piranport.book.torpedoes.basics.wire: $(bold)Wire-guided torpedoes:$() after launching a wire-guided torpedo (e.g. 533mm wire-guided, G7e wire type) you automatically enter the guidance view — steer it with your look direction (pitch + yaw). Exit the view to return to your ship; the torpedo keeps its last heading.$(br2)Any loaded tube can fire; a partially loaded launcher fires whatever is chambered.
piranport.book.torpedoes.named.p1: Multiple torpedo variants exist, each with unique damage, range, and speed.$(br)$(br)$(bold)533mm Series:$() Standard, Magnetic (magnetic fuze), Acoustic (homing), Wire-Guided (press $(bold)[9]/[0]$() to steer manually).$(br)$(br)$(bold)German G7 Series:$() G7a standard/magnetic, G7e electric magnetic/acoustic/wire-guided.
piranport.book.torpedoes.named.p2: $(bold)US MK Series:$() MK14 standard, MK16/MK17 hydrogen peroxide, MK27 acoustic.$(br)$(br)$(bold)Japanese Series:$() Type 91 610mm, Type 93 Mk1 high-speed / Mk3 long-range (oxygen torpedoes), Type 95 530mm/610mm submarine torpedoes, Type 0 720mm heavy torpedo.$(br)$(br)Hover over a torpedo item to view its specific damage/range/speed stats.
